prerequisites: Basic knowledge of technical mechanics (statics, tension-compression stress, bending and torsion of straight beams, buckling, free and forced vibrations, basic knowledge of control engineering such as transfer functions, basic mathematical knowledge (vector and matrix calculus, differential and integral calculus, linear differential equations))

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basics for detailed, accurate strength calculations of complex components and for the description of movements of dynamic systems, as well as the interactions between acting forces and moments and the resulting movements. They know the basics of elastostatics and elasticity theory as well as kinematics and kinetics of spatial movements, building upon the mechanics modules of the Bachelor's degree programs.

Students have an in-depth theoretical background knowledge to calculate simple spatial mechanical systems and to understand, use sensibly, and potentially further develop current tools of FEM, fatigue strength analysis, and multibody simulation. They can analyze the vibration behavior of components and develop problem solutions.

Students can describe, calculate, and evaluate arbitrary spatial stress and deformation states and interpret complex calculation results from modern software responsibly and with professional qualification. They are able to perform vibration analyses even on complex structures.
Students can prepare results of selected analyses and calculations, present and discuss them in groups, and conduct, document, and evaluate laboratory experiments in teams.

syllabus_topics: Vibration-optimized design of components using FEM
Experimental vibration analysis using transfer functions
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam; the duration is defined by the valid study regulations. An ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of 3 experiments. The prerequisites for earning ECTS credits are based on these performances.
